AJ: Thanks for making time, Rebecca. Walk me through where the hours go at Harbor & Pine right now.
Rebecca: Honestly? Billing. We're a six-attorney estate planning firm. Every month-end I spend two full days chasing unpaid invoices. Clients forget, the trust accounts need reconciling, and I'm writing the same polite reminder email forty times.
AJ: What does a reminder look like today?
Rebecca: I pull an aging report out of Clio, sort by 30, 60, 90 days, then write each client by hand. The 90-day ones get a firmer note and I cc the attorney. Some clients prefer a phone call, which I note in a spreadsheet.
AJ: And after the reminder?
Rebecca: If they pay, I mark it. If they reply with a question, it usually goes to Mark, our managing partner, and it sits in his inbox for a week.
AJ: What would a great Monday look like?
Rebecca: I'd come in and the aging report is already done, the reminders are drafted in our voice, and anything that needs Mark is in one short list for him. I would still want to approve anything going to a client — these are grieving families sometimes, tone matters.
AJ: Got it. Anything else eating time?
Rebecca: Intake follow-ups, but your Iris is already covering that. Oh, and every Friday Mark wants a one-page cash summary: collected this week, outstanding, who's at risk.
AJ: Perfect. So a billing coordinator: Monday aging and drafted reminders, a Friday cash summary for Mark, and replies routed to the right person.
Rebecca: Exactly. If that saves me those two days a month, it pays for itself.
